html:
The Mataram Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom in central Java, founded in the late 16th century near today's Yogyakarta. Under Sultan Agung, who ruled from 1613 to 1645, it conquered most of Java.

Sultan Agung twice besieged the Dutch fort of Batavia, in 1628 and 1629, but failed. He blended Islam with Javanese court tradition and created the Javanese calendar still in use.

Later rulers turned to the Dutch East India Company for help in civil wars and lost land to it. In 1755 Mataram was split into Yogyakarta and Surakarta. Their courts, such as the Kraton of Yogyakarta, survive, and the Sultan of Yogyakarta is still the governor of his province.
